title: Customer engagement platforms for SaaS in 2026: 10 tools, sorted by the channel they work in
summary: Compare ten customer engagement platforms for SaaS across in-product guidance, support, and lifecycle messaging. See where each tool fits, what your team manages, and which channels it covers.
body_markdown:
Ask a few people what a customer engagement platform is and you'll get different answers. A lifecycle marketer pictures email and push campaigns. Someone in support pictures the chat inbox. A product manager pictures tours and checklists inside the app. None of them are wrong, they're just describing different products that ended up under the same label.


We compare ten of those tools below, starting with where they reach users and what they help them do. We make Frigade and list it first, so read that entry knowing that.


Tool Where it reaches users What your team does Best for


Frigade Inside the product Connect the product and review generated guidance; build native Engage flows SaaS whose users get stuck mid-workflow


Pendo Inside the product Manage guides, feature tags, and analytics Teams already on Pendo analytics


Appcues Inside the product Build and target experiences in a visual editor Product teams managing onboarding


Userpilot Inside the product; email Build flows and segments; configure analytics PLG teams combining onboarding and analytics


Chameleon Inside the product Configure experiences, styling, and targeting Teams that want control over in-app styling


Userflow Inside the product Build or generate flows, review, and publish Teams that want a fast, polished builder


Intercom Messenger and inbox Maintain support content; configure Fin and procedures Support-led teams that live in chat


HubSpot Email, chat, help desk Build workflows on the CRM record Go-to-market teams standardized on HubSpot


Customer.io Email, push, SMS, in-app messages Build event-triggered campaigns Lifecycle messaging off product events


Braze Push, email, SMS, in-app messages Build cross-channel campaigns Consumer and mobile-first apps


## What is a customer engagement platform?


A customer engagement platform helps you communicate with users based on their behavior and track what happens next. In B2B SaaS, that can mean bringing someone back to the product or helping them finish a task once they're there.


The channels overlap. A lifecycle tool can use product events to send an email about unfinished setup, and some also send in-app messages. For a user already struggling with that setup, compare the help each tool provides on the screen: a message, a prepared tour, or guidance through the task.


## 1. Frigade


[Frigade Assistant](https://frigade.com/) learns your software by using it. It signs in, works through workflows, and re-learns the product as it changes. Users get answers, live walkthroughs, and help taking action in the product they already have open. It can also introduce a feature, help someone finish setup, or offer guidance when a workflow stalls. Your team doesn't need to write a tour for that guidance.


[Frigade Engage](https://frigade.com/engage) covers flows you want written exactly: checklists, announcements, and surveys built as React components in your codebase. Those components can use your design system.[Simplify](https://frigade.com/case-studies/simplify) runs 23 flows this way, and[Morning Consult](https://frigade.com/case-studies/morning-consult) reuses flows so product can launch them without engineering. The Assistant has separate controls for its logo, colors, typography, and position.


Engage is free for up to 250 monthly active users; Growth is $300 a month with 2,500 included. The Assistant starts at $1,000 a month.[Valley](https://frigade.com/case-studies/valley) uses the Assistant and saw support tickets drop after launch.


Frigade fits products where users need help completing workflows. Your team still installs the SDK, connects the product and documentation, and reviews responses before rollout. It doesn't send email or push, so you'll need another tool to reach users who stop logging in.


## 2. Pendo


[Pendo](https://frigade.com/compare/pendo) combines product analytics with in-app guides. You can see which features go unused and target guidance at the people who haven't found them. It makes sense if your team already uses Pendo's analytics.


We find the guides less polished than the analytics. If guidance is your main reason to buy, try building a guide on your own product before committing to the broader platform. Check what needs updating when you change the elements it targets. Pendo offers a free tier;[paid plans require a quote](https://www.pendo.io/pricing/) .


## 3. Appcues


[Appcues](https://frigade.com/compare/appcues) lets product teams build checklists, modals, and tooltip tours in a visual editor. It's a fit for teams that want direct control over an onboarding sequence. Appcues also offers AI-assisted experience creation.


The editor is mature, though we find customization beyond light theming cumbersome. Changes to the UI elements a flow targets can require updates.[Pricing](https://www.appcues.com/pricing) depends on monthly active users, installations, and published experiences.


## 4. Userpilot


[Userpilot](https://frigade.com/compare/userpilot) combines onboarding flows, checklists, surveys, a resource center, and product analytics. It also supports email. That breadth suits PLG teams that want to manage onboarding and measure the funnel in one place, though there is more to learn and configure.


[Starter begins at $299 a month](https://userpilot.com/pricing/) for up to 2,000 monthly active users. Growth, from $849 a month, adds advanced analytics, the resource center, and email. If you already pay for analytics elsewhere, weigh that overlap before adding another tool.


## 5. Chameleon


[Chameleon](https://frigade.com/compare/chameleon) provides tours, tooltips, microsurveys, launchers, and banners, with styling and targeting controls. Teams that want to manage how their in-app experiences look should consider it. Shared themes, custom CSS, and Copilot can help with that work.


[Plans differ in both features and usage limits](https://www.chameleon.io/plans) . Startup starts at $279 a month for 2,000 monthly tracked users, Pro at $750 for 5,000, and Growth at $1,250 for 5,000, billed annually.


## 6. Userflow


[Userflow](https://frigade.com/compare/userflow) offers a fast, polished builder for flows, checklists, resource centers, surveys, launchers, and banners. Its[FlowAI tools](https://www.userflow.com/) can also generate flows from your product and apply brand styling.


It suits teams that want a visual editor alongside AI-assisted creation. Pricing scales with monthly active users, so include expected user growth in your budget.


## 7. Intercom


Intercom combines a support inbox and in-app messenger with[Fin](https://frigade.com/compare/fin) , its AI agent. It also offers product tours and in-app messages. Support teams already using Intercom can keep chat, help content, and AI in one place.


Fin answers from support content and can use configured[Procedures](https://www.intercom.com/help/en/articles/12495167-fin-procedures-explained) and Data connectors to work with other systems. That setup differs from Frigade learning the product by using it. Compare them on the tasks your users need to complete. Some of our customers use Frigade for in-product AI and Intercom for human chat.


## 8. HubSpot


[HubSpot](https://frigade.com/compare/hubspot) brings CRM, marketing automation, and the Service Hub help desk together. Email sequences, workflows, and chat use the same contact record as sales.


It's a practical choice if your go-to-market teams already run on HubSpot. If users also need guidance through your product's UI, evaluate that separately; the CRM and help desk serve a different purpose.


## 9. Customer.io


Customer.io sends email, push, SMS, and in-app messages based on[events from your product](https://docs.customer.io/journeys/types-of-campaigns-and-broadcasts/) . You might remind someone to invite a teammate or follow up before their trial ends.


It suits teams that want lifecycle campaigns a marketer can edit. Its in-app messages also reach people already using the product. Check whether a message is enough for the task you're trying to help them complete, or whether they need guided steps.


## 10. Braze


Braze combines push, email, SMS, and in-app messaging with campaign orchestration and segmentation. Its breadth is useful for consumer and mobile products running campaigns across several channels.


For a B2B team running a few lifecycle campaigns, compare the features you'll use with the work of operating them. A dedicated lifecycle team has different requirements from someone fitting campaigns around other responsibilities.


## How to actually pick


Start with a task users aren't completing. If they never return, compare how you can reach them. If they return and get stuck, compare the help available inside the product. Some platforms cover both needs.


For in-product guidance, test one workflow with each shortlisted tool. Build or generate the guidance, check how it fits your interface, and change a relevant part of the UI. See what still works and what your team needs to update.


Frigade Assistant learns the product and generates guidance from that knowledge; Engage gives you control over deliberately authored flows. Include setup, review, ongoing maintenance, and usage limits in the cost comparison. A trial on your own product will tell you more than the feature list alone.


## FAQ


**What is the best customer engagement platform for SaaS in 2026?**


Start with the problem you need to solve. Customer.io, HubSpot, and Braze are options for lifecycle messaging. For onboarding and help inside the product, compare Frigade, Pendo, Appcues, Userpilot, Chameleon, Userflow, and Intercom. Several cover multiple channels, so compare the guidance they provide and the work your team does to run them.


**What is the difference between a customer engagement platform and a digital adoption platform?**


A[digital adoption platform](https://frigade.com/glossary/digital-adoption-platform) focuses on helping people use software through tours, tooltips, checklists, and contextual help. Customer engagement platform is a broader term that also covers lifecycle messaging through email, push, SMS, and chat. Some platforms provide both messaging and in-product guidance.


**Which customer engagement tools work inside the product?**


Frigade, Pendo, Appcues, Userpilot, Chameleon, and Userflow provide in-product guidance. Intercom offers a messenger and product tours, while Customer.io and Braze support in-app messages. Frigade Assistant learns the product by using it and generates guidance from that knowledge. Several other tools also offer AI-assisted creation; compare how the guidance is produced and maintained.


**Do I need both a lifecycle tool and an in-app tool?**


You may need both if you want to reach inactive users and help people complete tasks inside the product. First check what your existing tools cover. A platform with several messaging channels may cover your needs, or you may want a separate tool for product guidance.
